newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale prepared to talk on grain exports to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Goodale prepared to talk on grain exports to U.S.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said on Tuesday he was prepared to hold limited talks with the United States over complaints from U.S. farmers about Canadian grain exports.
But Goodale said the talks would only be to set the record straight and not to discuss reinstating limits on Canadian grain exports.

"The United States has been saying they may want consultations. We've always been prepared on any trade issue to sit down and talk about things with the United States, as long as the discussion is based on hard facts, and not on distorted rhetoric or political hotspots," Goodale said.
"It has to be a factual discussion, not an exaggerated discussion. And secondly, we are not interested in any process that leads to limitations," he told reporters.
Last week, North Dakota farmers renewed their call for U.S. officials to block Canadian grain exports to the United States.
U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshevsky told North Dakota farmers she was concerned that the United States should not become "a dumping ground for (Canada's) industry overhang."

"The arithmetic just does not support the case that certain spokespersons in the United States are trying to make," he said, noting that grain flows to the United States were artificially low last year, but this year's higher volumes are not unusual.
"There is no factual basis whatsoever for an allegation that Canadian grain movement into the U.S. marketplace is at all disruptive or unusual," Goodale said.
Any talks with U.S. representatives would be only to "straighten the record" and not to give in to demands that Canada reduce its exports, he said.
